How to use this calculator

  1. Enter age, target zone.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How target heart rate is calculated

Estimated maximum = 220−age. Moderate zone is 50–70% and vigorous zone is 70–85% of that estimate, following American Heart Association guidance. At age 40, estimated maximum is 180 bpm; the moderate zone is about 90–126 bpm.

Age-predicted max=220−age; moderate=50–70%, vigorous=70–85%.
A worked example

At age 40, estimated maximum is 180 bpm; the moderate zone is about 90–126 bpm.

Assumptions & useful context

Broad averages only; medication and health conditions can change safe targets.

Health calculations are estimates for education. They cannot diagnose a condition or replace a clinician’s assessment. Individual needs vary, especially during pregnancy, illness and growth.

American Heart Association: Target heart-rate zones

Frequently asked questions

Is 220 minus age exact?

No. It is a population rule of thumb with substantial individual variation.

What if I take heart medication or have a heart condition?

Ask a healthcare professional for an appropriate exercise range.
